clue.text: Piece of luggage I dance round

indicators.note: the dance word goes round the I, so the I sits inside it

parts.note: a valse is the French name for a waltz, a dance

explanation.surface: A traveller twirls around a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A valise is a small travelling bag or suitcase.

clue.text: Badly tailored heathen

indicators.note: badly made, so the letters of the word tailored are put together wrongly

explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, which a believer would call a heathen.

clue.text: A splash-down of little or no consequence

definitions.meaning: a single drip falling into the sea, taken literally
an idiom for an amount too small to matter

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes a drip landing in the sea and idiomatically means an insignificant amount.

clue.text: Willing to try out another blend of tea

parts.note: to try out something is to test it

indicators.note: the letters of tea are mixed into a different blend

explanation.surface: Someone keen to sample a new mix of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' is not eager here: it means having made a will. 'another blend of' rearranges TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A testate person has left a valid will, so is literally will-ing.

clue.text: Clearly most unpopular with the electorate

definitions.text: Clearly most unpopular with the electorate

parts.words: Clearly most unpopular with the electorate
parts.note: describes a candidate or party ranked last in a survey of voting intentions

explanation.definitionFit: Coming last in an opinion survey shows the voters like you least.

clue.text: We go after ducks on Lake Ontario

indicators.note: the words we go come after the ducks

parts.note: a duck is a zero in cricket, so ducks are O's
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two of us head off following some waterfowl on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' looks like birds on the lake, but in cricket a duck is a score of nought, written O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oswego is a city in New York State on the shore of Lake Ontario.

clue.text: Marginal advantage

parts.note: a slight lead over a rival, also read as something at the margin or rim

explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand by a small amount is having a slight lead, while the margin of anything is its rim.

clue.text: Rural dean holding an African coin

indicators.note: the cleric's letters hold the other word inside them

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for a rural dean in the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country clergyman pockets a coin from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The rand is the currency unit of South Africa.

clue.text: Appropriate fee to be paid

definitions.meaning: fitting, deserved, as in given its proper weight
a charge owed, as in membership subscriptions

explanation.definitionFit: Due means fitting or proper, and dues are charges owed to a club or body.

clue.text: In a position to shoot?

parts.note: reads like a marksman ready to fire, but means a footballer legally placed to have a shot at goal

explanation.definitionFit: A player not offside is legally placed and may shoot at goal.

clue.text: Venice's busiest pedestrian crossing

parts.note: sounds like a zebra crossing on a road, but means the famous bridge over the Grand Canal

explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the oldest and best-known bridge spanning the Grand Canal in Venice.

clue.text: Edward went round there to put on a picket

indicators.note: the name's letters go around the other word, holding it inside

parts.note: Ted is a common short form of the name Edward
taken as written

explanation.surface: Edward walked over to join a strike line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picket' suggests strikers, but here it is a stake to which an animal is tied.
explanation.definitionFit: A picket is a pointed stake, and an animal tied to one is secured by a rope.

clue.text: Cut down expenditure on exotic goods

definitions.text: Cut down expenditure on exotic goods

parts.words: Cut down expenditure on exotic goods
parts.note: describes a government policy of limiting foreign purchases

explanation.definitionFit: Limiting goods bought from abroad is a protectionist trade measure.

clue.text: Too young a child to add up?

definitions.meaning: a very small child, a toddler
to total a column of figures, as in sum up

explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child, and to tot up is to total figures.

clue.text: Hurried back with speed to give an account of events

indicators.note: the word for hurried is written in the reverse direction

parts.note: hurried means ran
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Someone rushed home quickly to tell what had happened.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story or recount happenings.

clue.text: A party that spells trouble

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Produces results

explanation.definitionFit: To effect something is to bring it about, and effects are outcomes or consequences.

clue.text: What peers should get as remuneration?

definitions.text: What peers should get as remuneration?

parts.words: What peers should get as remuneration?
parts.note: peers suggests lords, but here means people who are equals, deserving the same wages

explanation.definitionFit: People of the same standing deserve identical wages, the principle of the same reward for the same work.

clue.text: Going into a study group he conflicts violently with opinions expressed

indicators.note: the pronoun goes into the group word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a class is a group of students studying together
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man joining a seminar argues fiercely with everyone's views.
explanation.definitionFit: Clashes are fierce disagreements, especially of views.

clue.text: A pharmacopoeia that tells us how to take?

definitions.text: A pharmacopoeia that tells us how to take?

parts.words: A pharmacopoeia that tells us how to take?
parts.note: a book of medicines, with the twist that a raised glass and a toast tell drinkers how to keep well

explanation.definitionFit: A handbook on staying well would list remedies, and the phrase also puns on a drinker's toast.

clue.text: Sad reflection about everything we get from American TV

indicators.note: the turned word goes about the other piece, enclosing it
a mirror image, so the word sad is read the other way round

parts.note: taken as written
all means everything

explanation.surface: A gloomy thought on all that comes over from US television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sad' looks like the mood of the surface but is fodder; DALLAS is the American TV soap about a Texan oil family.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas was a long-running American television soap opera about an oil family.

clue.text: Prim and proper Spanish girl guide

definitions.text: Prim and proper Spanish girl guide

parts.words: Prim and proper Spanish girl guide
parts.note: suggests a scout leader, but means a strict older woman who chaperones a young lady in Spain

explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as governess and chaperone to girls in a Spanish family.

clue.text: Gathers for prayers, maybe

definitions.meaning: short prayers set for particular days in church services

explanation.definitionFit: To collect is to gather, and a collect is a short liturgical prayer.

clue.text: High distinction conferred on an oil-rich state

indicators.note: in this down clue the honour is placed on top of the next word

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a high British honour

explanation.surface: An honour is awarded to a wealthy petroleum nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a Gulf sultanate whose economy rests on oil.

clue.text: By no means a big shot

definitions.text: By no means a big shot

parts.words: By no means a big shot
parts.note: sounds like a lowly person, but means a small piece of ammunition

explanation.definitionFit: A pellet is a small piece of shot fired from an air gun or shotgun.

clue.text: Parental couple ringing an international waterway

indicators.note: the parents' letters ring the other word, holding it inside

parts.note: pa and ma, the two parents
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum and dad phone a famous canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

clue.text: At heart we feel it's not easy to grasp

indicators.note: the letters are tucked away within the words we feel

explanation.surface: Deep down we sense something slippery.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is notoriously slippery and hard to hold.

clue.text: Inane king who won fame as a composer

annotationWithheld.why: Inane king who won fame as a composer (4): ARNE needs A,N,E from INANE with R inserted, but no word signals dropping IN; likely an OCR or print slip
annotationWithheld.clue: Inane king who won fame as a composer
